questions.prompt: What does “solubility of salt is 36 g at 20 °C” mean?
options: 36 g of salt dissolves in 1 L of water
36 g of salt is the most that dissolves in 100 g of water at 20 °C
questions.explain: Solubility is per 100 g of water at a stated temperature.

questions.prompt: A point lies below the solubility curve. The solution is…
options: supersaturated with solid at the bottom
questions.explain: Below the curve, more solute could still dissolve.

questions.prompt: Potassium nitrate’s solubility is 106 g at 60 °C and 32 g at 20 °C. A saturated solution in 100 g of water is cooled from 60 °C to 20 °C. How many grams of crystals form?
Which statement about stirring a saturated solution is correct?
options: Stirring always turns it into a colloid
Stirring does not make more solute dissolve
questions.explain: Stirring speeds up dissolving but cannot raise the maximum amount.

questions.prompt: At 40 °C, 64 g of a salt dissolves in 100 g of water. How much will dissolve in 50 g of water at 40 °C?
questions.explain: Half the water dissolves half as much: 32 g.

questions.prompt: For most solids, what happens to solubility as the temperature rises?
questions.explain: Most solid solubility curves slope upwards (some, like salt, only slightly).

questions.prompt: Put the steps for making pure copper sulfate crystals in order.
steps: Dissolve impure copper sulfate in hot water until saturated
Filter the hot solution to remove insoluble impurities
Leave the filtrate to cool slowly
Filter off the crystals and dry them on filter paper
questions.explain: Crystallisation: dissolve hot, filter, cool, collect.

questions.prompt: A solution of 50 g of a solid in 100 g of water at 70 °C is cooled to 30 °C, where the solubility is 25 g. What mass of crystals forms?
questions.explain: 50 − 25 = 25 g (assuming it was saturated or unsaturated with 50 g dissolved at 70 °C).
